title: Circumference and Area of Circles
seo_title: Grade 7 Circumference and Area of Circles Worksheets (TEKS 7.9B, STAAR)
standard_text: 7.5B describe π as the ratio of the circumference of a circle to its diameter; 7.8C use models to determine the approximate formulas for the circumference and area of a circle and connect the models to the actual formulas; 7.9B determine the circumference and area of circles
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 circle worksheets for Texas TEKS 7.5B, 7.8C and 7.9B: radius, diameter and π, circumference, area, working backward and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: r = 5 cm: C = 31.4 cm, A = 78.5 cm².
body_html:
How to think about it

  • π is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter, about 3.14 or 22/7.
  • Circumference: C = πd = 2πr.
  • Area: A = πr². Cut a circle into thin wedges and line them up: they make a shape close to a parallelogram with base πr and height r.
  • The diameter is twice the radius.

Examples

Example

r = 5 cm

C = 2 × 3.14 × 5

A = 3.14 × 5²

Answer: C = 31.4 cm, A = 78.5 cm²

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using the diameter in A = πr²Halve the diameter to get r first.
Mixing up C and ACircumference is a length (cm); area is square units (cm²).
Squaring before halvingr = d ÷ 2, then square r.

faq.a: Describe π as the ratio of the circumference of a circle to its diameter.
Determine the circumference and area of circles.
Use models to determine the approximate formulas for the circumference and area of a circle and connect the models to the actual formulas.
Use what the problem says. 22/7 is handy when the radius is a multiple of 7.

items.q: A circle has a radius of 4 cm. What is its diameter?
items.e: The diameter goes all the way across: d = 2r = 2 × 4 = 8 cm. Not 2: that halves the radius.

items.q: A circle has a radius of 9 cm. What is its diameter?
items.e: The diameter goes all the way across: d = 2r = 2 × 9 = 18 cm. Not 4.5: that halves the radius.

items.q: A circle has a radius of 2.5 cm. What is its diameter?
items.e: The diameter goes all the way across: d = 2r = 2 × 2.5 = 5 cm. Not 1.25: that halves the radius.

items.q: A circle has a radius of 15 cm. What is its diameter?
items.e: The diameter goes all the way across: d = 2r = 2 × 15 = 30 cm. Not 7.5: that halves the radius.

items.q: A circle has a diameter of 10 in. What is its radius?
items.e: The radius is half the diameter: r = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 in.

items.q: A circle has a diameter of 7 in. What is its radius?
items.e: The radius is half the diameter: r = 7 ÷ 2 = 3.5 in.

items.q: A circle has a diameter of 24 in. What is its radius?
items.e: The radius is half the diameter: r = 24 ÷ 2 = 12 in.

items.q: A circle has a diameter of 3.6 in. What is its radius?
items.e: The radius is half the diameter: r = 3.6 ÷ 2 = 1.8 in.

items.q: Which formula gives the circumference of a circle?
items.e: Circumference is the distance around: C = 2πr, or C = πd. πr² is the area.

items.q: Which formula gives the area of a circle?
items.e: Area is the space inside: A = πr². 2πr and πd give the circumference.

items.q: What does π mean?
c: The circumference divided by the diameter
The area divided by the radius
The diameter divided by the radius
items.e: For every circle, circumference ÷ diameter is the same number, π ≈ 3.14.

items.q: A circle has circumference 31.4 cm and diameter 10 cm. What is circumference ÷ diameter?
items.e: 31.4 ÷ 10 = 3.14, which is about π.

items.q: A circle has a radius of 3 m. What is its circumference in terms of π?
items.e: C = 2πr = 2 × π × 3 = 6π m. Not 9π: that is the area formula.

items.q: A circle has a radius of 5 m. What is its circumference in terms of π?
items.e: C = 2πr = 2 × π × 5 = 10π m. Not 25π: that is the area formula.

items.q: A circle has a radius of 8 m. What is its circumference in terms of π?
items.e: C = 2πr = 2 × π × 8 = 16π m. Not 64π: that is the area formula.

items.q: A circle has a radius of 11 m. What is its circumference in terms of π?
items.e: C = 2πr = 2 × π × 11 = 22π m. Not 121π: that is the area formula.

items.q: A circle has a radius of 4 ft. What is its area in terms of π?
items.e: A = πr² = π × 4² = 16π ft². Not 64π: that squares the diameter.

items.q: A circle has a radius of 6 ft. What is its area in terms of π?
items.e: A = πr² = π × 6² = 36π ft². Not 144π: that squares the diameter.

items.q: A circle has a radius of 10 ft. What is its area in terms of π?
items.e: A = πr² = π × 10² = 100π ft². Not 400π: that squares the diameter.

items.q: A circle has a radius of 7 ft. What is its area in terms of π?
items.e: A = πr² = π × 7² = 49π ft². Not 196π: that squares the diameter.

items.e: A = πr² = 3.14 × 5² = 3.14 × 25 = 78.5 in². Not 31.4: that multiplies r by 2 instead of squaring it.

sets.title: Working backward and parts of circles

items.q: A circle has circumference 31.4 cm. What is its diameter? Use 3.14 for π.
items.e: C = πd, so d = C ÷ π = 31.4 ÷ 3.14 = 10 cm. Not 5: that is the radius.

items.q: A circle has circumference 62.8 cm. What is its diameter? Use 3.14 for π.
items.e: C = πd, so d = C ÷ π = 62.8 ÷ 3.14 = 20 cm. Not 10: that is the radius.

items.q: A circle has circumference 18.84 cm. What is its diameter? Use 3.14 for π.
items.e: C = πd, so d = C ÷ π = 18.84 ÷ 3.14 = 6 cm. Not 3: that is the radius.

items.q: A circle has circumference 94.2 cm. What is its diameter? Use 3.14 for π.
items.e: C = πd, so d = C ÷ π = 94.2 ÷ 3.14 = 30 cm. Not 15: that is the radius.

items.q: A circle has circumference 25.12 m. What is its radius? Use 3.14 for π.
A circle has circumference 43.96 m. What is its radius? Use 3.14 for π.
A circle has circumference 62.8 m. What is its radius? Use 3.14 for π.
A circle has area 78.5 ft². What is its radius? Use 3.14 for π.
items.e: A = πr², so r² = 78.5 ÷ 3.14 = 25. Then r = 5 ft, because 5 × 5 = 25.

items.q: A circle has area 12.56 ft². What is its radius? Use 3.14 for π.
items.e: A = πr², so r² = 12.56 ÷ 3.14 = 4. Then r = 2 ft, because 2 × 2 = 4.

items.q: A circle has area 314 ft². What is its radius? Use 3.14 for π.
items.e: A = πr², so r² = 314 ÷ 3.14 = 100. Then r = 10 ft, because 10 × 10 = 100.

items.q: A circle has area 28.26 ft². What is its radius? Use 3.14 for π.
items.e: A = πr², so r² = 28.26 ÷ 3.14 = 9. Then r = 3 ft, because 3 × 3 = 9.

items.q: A circle has circumference 18π cm. What is its radius?
items.e: C = 2πr = 18π, so r = 9 cm.

items.q: A circle has area 49π in². What is its diameter?
items.e: A = πr² = 49π, so r² = 49 and r = 7. The diameter is 2 × 7 = 14 in.

items.q: Find the area of a semicircle with radius 4 cm. Use 3.14 for π.
items.e: A full circle has area 3.14 × 4² = 50.24 square centimeters. A semicircle is half of it: 25.12 square centimeters.

items.q: Find the area of a semicircle with radius 10 cm. Use 3.14 for π.
items.e: A full circle has area 3.14 × 10² = 314 square centimeters. A semicircle is half of it: 157 square centimeters.

items.q: Find the area of a quarter circle with radius 6 cm. Use 3.14 for π.
items.e: A full circle has area 3.14 × 6² = 113.04 square centimeters. A quarter circle is one quarter of it: 28.26 square centimeters.

items.q: Find the area of a quarter circle with radius 2 cm. Use 3.14 for π.
items.e: A full circle has area 3.14 × 2² = 12.56 square centimeters. A quarter circle is one quarter of it: 3.14 square centimeters.

items.q: Find the distance around a semicircle with diameter 10 m (the curved part plus the straight edge). Use 3.14 for π.
items.e: Curved part = half of πd = 3.14 × 10 ÷ 2 = 15.7 m. Add the diameter: 15.7 + 10 = 25.7 m. Not 15.7 m: that leaves out the straight edge.

items.q: If the radius of a circle doubles, what happens to its area?
items.e: A = πr². With 2r, A = π(2r)² = 4πr². The circumference only doubles.

items.q: If the radius of a circle doubles, what happens to its circumference?
items.e: C = 2πr. With 2r, C = 2π(2r) = 2 × 2πr, which is twice as long.

items.q: A bike wheel has a diameter of 26 inches. How far does the bike go in one full turn of the wheel? Use 3.14 for π.
items.e: One turn = the circumference: C = πd = 3.14 × 26 = 81.64 in.

items.q: A round pizza has a diameter of 14 inches. What is its area? Use 3.14 for π.
items.e: r = 7 in. A = 3.14 × 7² = 3.14 × 49 = 153.86 in². Not 615.44: that uses the diameter.

items.q: A circular garden has a radius of 5 m. How much fencing goes around it? Use 3.14 for π.
items.e: Fencing goes around, so find the circumference: 2 × 3.14 × 5 = 31.4 m.

items.q: A sprinkler waters a circle with a radius of 6 ft. What area of lawn does it water? Use 3.14 for π.
A circular track has a diameter of 100 m. How far is one lap? Use 3.14 for π.
items.e: One lap is the circumference: 3.14 × 100 = 314 m.

items.q: Owen walks around a circular pond 3 times. The pond has a radius of 20 m. How far does he walk? Use 3.14 for π.
A clock's minute hand is 10 cm long. How far does its tip travel in 1 hour? Use 3.14 for π.
items.e: In 1 hour the tip goes all the way around a circle with radius 10 cm: 2 × 3.14 × 10 = 62.8 cm.

items.q: A round table top has a radius of 3 ft. Paint costs $2 per square foot. What does it cost to paint the top? Use 3.14 for π.
A circular rug has an area of 50.24 ft². What is its radius? Use 3.14 for π.
A wheel has a circumference of 188.4 cm. What is its diameter? Use 3.14 for π.
A trampoline has a diameter of 12 ft. A cover must go over the top. What area must it cover? Use 3.14 for π.
A can of soup has a label that wraps around it once. The can has a diameter of 7 cm. How long is the label? Use 3.14 for π.
items.e: The label goes around the can: C = 3.14 × 7 = 21.98 cm.

items.q: A circular window has a radius of 1.5 ft. What is its area? Use 3.14 for π.
A dog is tied to a post with a 9 m rope. What area can the dog reach? Use 3.14 for π.
items.e: The dog can reach a circle with radius 9 m: A = 3.14 × 81 = 254.34 square meters.

items.q: A Ferris wheel has a radius of 25 m. How far does a seat travel in one full turn? Use 3.14 for π.
A semicircle window sits on top of a door. The window's diameter is 4 ft. What is the area of the window? Use 3.14 for π.
items.e: A full circle with r = 2 ft has area 3.14 × 4 = 12.56 ft². Half of it is 6.28 ft².

items.q: A 12-inch pizza and an 8-inch pizza are both round. About how much more area does the 12-inch pizza have? Use 3.14 for π.
A square is 10 cm on each side. A circle with diameter 10 cm is cut out of it. What area is left? Use 3.14 for π.
items.e: Square: 10 × 10 = 100 square centimeters. Circle: 3.14 × 5² = 78.5 square centimeters. Left: 100 − 78.5 = 21.5 square centimeters.

items.q: A wheel turns 50 times. Its radius is 0.3 m. How far does it roll? Use 3.14 for π.
A circle's circumference is 6.28 m. What is its area? Use 3.14 for π.
items.e: C = 2πr = 6.28, so r = 1 m. A = 3.14 × 1² = 3.14 square meters.
